Samuel Pepys, The Diary, edited by Henry B. Wheatley.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/samuel-pepys/the-diary

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Samuel Pepys, the author, died 1703 (Wikidata Q106143, P570 = 1703-05-26).
- Henry B. Wheatley, the editor, died 1917 (Wikidata Q5717646, P570 = 1917, 1917-04-30).
- Richard Griffin, the annotator, died 1858 (Wikidata Q7326083, P570 = 1858-03-13).

First publication of the text used: not stated in the facts (SE colophon: 'The Diary was written between 1659 and 1669 by Samuel Pepys.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the colophon gives no first-publication year. The Standard Ebooks rights statement below says the text is in the United States public domain, and that statement covers the United States side.
- Country of origin: every person named above died in 1917 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, whatever its country of first publication.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
